reden: Yes. The report explicitly flags the same reentrancy window in createCred/_createCredInternal: it calls buyShareCred, which refunds excess ETH (an external call) before credIdCounter is incremented and without a reentrancy guard, allowing re-entry into createCred and overwriting creds[credIdCounter]. Although the report frames the impact as ID corruption/stale merkle roots, it’s the identical root cause and code path exploited in H‑06 (re-entering during the refund while the cred is half‑initialized). Adding nonReentrant to createCred or reordering state updates (CEI) would fix both issues. The report also separately notes the refund-before-timestamp update reentrancy that enables immediate selling, which the H‑06 scenario leverages. Thus, same mechanism, same functions, and the same fix; only the impact elaboration differs.
